text: Complete reducibility means every stable submodule W has a stable complement Q, with W∩Q=0 and W+Q=V. This is the direct-summand criterion of [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). Over semirings the native predicate retains exactly this lattice-complement condition, without claiming unique decompositions. No dimension bound or canonical complement is imposed. Checks pass: [exists_isCompl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L117), [isCompletelyReducible_monoidAlgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L473).
Checks the complement accessor.
Checks the actual monoid-algebra family.

This constructor turns a supplied complement for each subcomodule into complete reducibility. The hypothesis includes both zero intersection and full sum of the underlying modules, exactly the direct-summand criterion in [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). No averaging operator, basis choice, finite-dimensionality or assumption that all ordinary module complements are stable is added. Checks pass: [exists_isCompl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L117), [isCompletelyReducible_of_subsingleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L140).
Checks recovery of the supplied property.
Checks the zero-module boundary case.

Complete reducibility supplies a stable complement to any specified subcomodule. The conclusion concerns the underlying module lattice, so it explicitly ensures trivial intersection and full span, as in [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). This is an existential accessor; it neither makes the complement unique nor claims that every module splitting respects the coaction. Checks pass: [of_exists_isCompl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L109), [projection_apply_of_mem_left](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L76).
Checks the converse packaging.
Checks the projection arising from a supplied stable complement.

If the only subcomodules are zero and the whole module, each is complemented by the other. This proves the complement criterion of [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101) directly, even over a commutative semiring. Unlike simplicity, the hypothesis permits the zero module, where bottom and top coincide; that boundary case remains correctly included. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_of_subsingleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L140), [isCompletelyReducible_of_isSimpleOrder](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L152).
Checks the permitted zero case.
Checks the nonzero simple case.

A module with just one element is the zero module, and its sole subcomodule is complemented by itself. Thus complete reducibility holds even though simplicity normally excludes zero. The source checks the same stable-complement condition as [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101), with no nontriviality or field assumption hidden in this semiring statement. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_of_forall_eq_bot_or_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L126), [exists_isCompl](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L117).
Checks the general two-boundary criterion.
Checks what complete reducibility supplies.

A simple subcomodule lattice has exactly the distinct elements zero and V. Complementing either by the other proves complete reducibility, agreeing with the elementary simple-representation case of [Milne §4.f](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). Here simplicity is a condition on stable subobjects, not on all underlying submodules or the coefficient coalgebra. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_of_forall_eq_bot_or_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L126), [isCompletelyReducible_of_subsingleton](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L140).
Checks the underlying complement argument.
Checks the separately allowed zero case.

Complete reducibility is equivalent to a colinear endomorphism projecting onto each stable W and fixing W pointwise, the projection version of [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). Over a commutative ring, flatness of C ensures the kernel of such a retraction is stable; that kernel supplies the reverse-direction complement. Idempotence follows from the stated conditions. Checks pass: [projection_apply_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L70), [projection_apply_of_mem_left](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Projection.lean#L76).
Checks the projection lands in W.
Checks it fixes W pointwise.

Linear reductivity requires every finite-dimensional comodule to be completely reducible, matching [Milne 12.52](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=259). The native definition applies to any coalgebra over a field; for a coordinate Hopf algebra it is the usual group property. Its explicit carrier universe is bookkeeping, later removed by transporting finite-dimensional spaces to coordinate spaces. Checks pass: [isLinearlyReductive_monoidAlgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L491), [not_isLinearlyReductive](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/AdditiveGroup/LinearlyReductive.lean#L48).
Checks the diagonalizable-coordinate positive family.
Checks the additive-group counterexample over every field.

Complete reducibility transfers through an order isomorphism of stable subobjects compatible with an order isomorphism of their underlying submodules. Order isomorphisms preserve zero, full modules, intersections and sums, hence preserve the complement criterion of [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). Compatibility is explicit: a bare correspondence between stable subobjects is not silently substituted. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_transport_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L267), [isCompletelyReducible_corestrict_iff_of_coalgEquiv](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L290).
Checks actual transport along a linear equivalence.
Checks actual coalgebra-equivalence corestriction.

Transporting the coaction along a linear equivalence preserves and reflects complete reducibility. Stable subobjects and their underlying module complements correspond under that same equivalence, giving the criterion in [Milne 4.17](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=101). The target coaction is specifically the transported one; an arbitrary linear equivalence between independently chosen comodules would not suffice. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_of_orderIso](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L243), [isCompletelyReducible](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L339).
Checks the compatible-order-isomorphism argument.
Checks the coordinate-space transport application.

Supplying complete reducibility for every finite-dimensional comodule constructs linear reductivity, exactly the universal condition in [Milne 12.52](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=259). Over the field, Module.Finite means finite-dimensional as a vector space, not that the carrier is a finite set. The carrier universe matches the hypothesis; no algebraic-group structure is required for this coalgebra predicate. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_sameUniverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L329), [isLinearlyReductive_monoidAlgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L491).
Checks application within the quantified universe.
Checks an actual family satisfying the definition.

Testing finite-dimensional comodules in the base field’s universe suffices for every carrier universe. A basis identifies V with kⁿ; transporting its coaction lets the hypothesis apply, and transporting complements back proves the result. This preserves the mathematical scope of [Milne 12.52](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=259); universe size contributes no extra restriction on representations. Checks pass: [isCompletelyReducible_transport_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L267), [isCompletelyReducible_sameUniverse](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L329).
Checks preservation under coordinate transport.
Checks the direct application after transport.

Every comodule over the coalgebra k[G] is completely reducible over a field, extending the weight decomposition of [Milne 12.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Apply an ordinary projection separately on each weight and project back to that weight; its kernel is a stable complement. G is only an indexing type and V may be infinite-dimensional. These are comodules, not group-algebra modules. Checks pass: [isLinearlyReductive_monoidAlgebra](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive.lean#L491), [weightProj_mem_subcomodule](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L550).
Checks the resulting linear-reductivity family.
Checks stable subobjects preserve every weight component.

An invariant vector in the image of a comodule morphism has an invariant preimage when its source is completely reducible and C is flat over a commutative ring. Complement the kernel, then reflect fixedness through the injective restriction. This is the invariant-lifting argument underlying [Milne 15.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=322), without requiring the whole morphism surjective. Checks pass: [mem_fixedSubcomodule_iff_of_injective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/Fixed.lean#L181), [map_fixedSubcomodule_of_isCompletelyReducible](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive/Fixed.lean#L101).
Checks reflection of fixedness using flatness.
Checks the resulting invariant-image equality.

For a linearly reductive coalgebra over a field, every invariant vector in a morphism’s image has an invariant preimage, even in infinite-dimensional comodules. Place one initial preimage inside a finite-dimensional subcomodule and apply complete reducibility there. This realizes the local-finiteness extension in [Milne 12.53(a)](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=259), with fixedness defined by the distinguished coefficient 1. Checks pass: [exists_finite_subcomodule_mem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Finite.lean#L141), [exists_fixed_preimage_of_isCompletelyReducible](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive/Fixed.lean#L58).
Checks the finite-dimensional containing subobject.
Checks lifting inside that subobject.

A surjective comodule morphism over a linearly reductive coalgebra remains surjective after restricting to invariant vectors. Choose an ordinary preimage and replace it by an invariant one. This is the exactness mechanism in [Milne 15.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=322); local finite-dimensionality permits arbitrary source and target dimensions, while linear reductivity remains a genuine hypothesis. Checks pass: [exists_fixed_preimage_of_isLinearlyReductive](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive/Fixed.lean#L159), [map_fixedSubcomodule_of_isLinearlyReductive](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive/Fixed.lean#L174).
Checks the invariant lift.
Checks the stronger invariant-image identity.

An invariant vector expressed as a finite sum of images under comodule morphisms admits such an expression using invariant preimages. Induction passes to the quotient by one image, then lifts the invariant remainder. This extends the invariant-lifting mechanism of [Milne 15.15](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=322); only indices in the specified finite set require invariant choices. Checks pass: [exists_fixed_preimage_of_isLinearlyReductive](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive/Fixed.lean#L159), [mkQ_eq_zero_iff](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Subcomodule/Quotient.lean#L233).
Checks the final invariant remainder lift.
Checks quotient-kernel membership used in the induction.

For a commutative Hopf algebra over a field, linear reductivity is equivalent to surjectivity on invariants for every surjection of finite-dimensional comodules. The converse lifts the identity through an internal Hom, producing an equivariant section, as in [Milne 15.15’s proof](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=323). No smoothness, reducedness, finite-type or characteristic-zero hypothesis is needed. Checks pass: [fixedMap_surjective_of_isLinearlyReductive](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearlyReductive/Fixed.lean#L182), [exists_rightInverse_of_linearHomPostcomp_fixedMap_surjective](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/LinearHom.lean#L271).
Checks the forward implication.
Checks lifting the identity yields a colinear section.

Every stable submodule of an R[G]-comodule contains all weight components of each of its vectors. The inclusion is colinear, hence commutes with coefficient extraction. This is the subobject form of the grading in [Milne 12.12–13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246); the source proves it over a commutative semiring without a field or finite-generation assumption. Checks pass: [map_weightProj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L514), [range_weightProj](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L564).
Checks naturality of the coefficient projections.
Checks each projection has the claimed weight-space image.

A finitely generated R[G]-comodule has only finitely many nonzero weight spaces. Its independent weight spaces span V, and finite generation confines this sum to finitely many summands. This extends the finite-dimensional grading picture in [Milne 12.13](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246) to commutative semirings; finite generation concerns the module, not the cardinality of its carrier. Checks pass: [iSup_weightSpace_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L398), [iSupIndep_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L407).
Checks weight spaces span the module.
Checks their independence.

On a vector of weight g, the endomorphism attached to an algebra map f:R[G]→A multiplies the scalar-extended vector by f([g]). The formula is a⊗v↦a·f([g])⊗v, matching the character action in [Milne 12.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). A monoid suffices here; the resulting endomorphism need not be invertible without group hypotheses. Checks pass: [baseChange_weightSpace_le_eigenspace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Semisimple.lean#L57), [iSup_eigenspace_endOfPoint_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Semisimple.lean#L102).
Checks the induced eigenvalue statement.
Checks these eigenvectors span after scalar extension.

After extension to a commutative ring K, the g-weight submodule lies in the eigenspace with eigenvalue f([g]). The pure-tensor action formula extends to its K-span, as predicted by [Milne 12.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Base change here means the image-generated submodule; no injective embedding or flatness of K over R is assumed. Checks pass: [endOfPoint_tmul_of_mem_weightSpace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L599), [iSup_baseChange_weightSpace_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Semisimple.lean#L80).
Checks the pure-tensor eigenvalue formula.
Checks the extended weight submodules span.

The scalar-extended weight submodules span K⊗_R V because each original vector is a finite sum of its weight components and tensors are generated by pure tensors. This is the base-change form of [Milne 12.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). The native semiring result needs no flatness, injectivity of scalar extension, or multiplication on the weight indexing type. Checks pass: [weightDecomposition_sum](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L284), [iSup_weightSpace_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Basic.lean#L398).
Checks reconstruction from finitely supported components.
Checks the original weight-space spanning identity.

Every scalar-extended weight submodule lies in an eigenspace for the point endomorphism, so their spanning property makes the sum of all eigenspaces equal the whole module. This implements the diagonal action of [Milne 12.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246) over a commutative target ring. Distinct weights may evaluate to the same eigenvalue at a particular point. Checks pass: [baseChange_weightSpace_le_eigenspace](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Semisimple.lean#L57), [iSup_baseChange_weightSpace_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Semisimple.lean#L80).
Checks the eigenvalue inclusion.
Checks spanning after extension.

Over a field K, the point endomorphism of an R[G]-comodule is semisimple because its eigenspaces span after scalar extension, as in the diagonal action of [Milne 12.12](https://www.jmilne.org/math/CourseNotes/iAG2022.pdf#page=246). Semisimple here means the associated K[X]-module is semisimple. Neither finite-dimensionality nor algebraic closedness is needed, and invertibility is not asserted for a monoid. Checks pass: [iSup_eigenspace_endOfPoint_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/Algebra/Coalgebra/Comodule/MonoidAlgebra/Semisimple.lean#L102), [isSemisimple_of_iSup_eigenspace_eq_top](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/36f24f5d94ccf25e167520cf4c0f1a028c064fb0/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/Eigenspace/Semisimple.lean#L51).
Checks the full eigenspace span.
Checks the K[X]-module semisimplicity implication.

This is the natural logarithm on positive real numbers. Lean extends it to negative inputs by taking the logarithm of their absolute value, and assigns log 0=0. Thus it is an even real function, not a complex logarithm; outside the positive axis, it is no longer an inverse of the exponential. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L44).

Exponentiating the logarithm of a positive real number returns that number. Strict positivity is essential to this formulation: for a negative input, Lean’s logarithm forgets the sign, so exponentiation returns its absolute value instead. At zero, log 0=0 gives exp(log 0)=1, not zero. The theorem makes neither of those excluded assertions. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L59).

Taking the natural logarithm of exp x returns x for every real x, including negative x and zero. No positivity assumption on x is needed: it is exp x, the input to logarithm, that is always positive. Consequently this identity stays entirely within the classical logarithm domain and does not use the assigned log-zero value. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L75).

Lean assigns the real logarithm the value zero at zero. This is a definition outside the classical positive domain, not the logarithm’s right-hand limit: as positive inputs approach zero, the classical logarithm tends to negative infinity. The assignment makes the function everywhere defined without placing infinity in the ordinary real number type. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L103).

The natural logarithm of 1 is zero, as in ordinary analysis, because exp 0=1. This identity concerns a positive input and therefore agrees directly with the classical inverse definition. With Lean’s global extension, however, a zero logarithm does not uniquely identify 1: zero and −1 also have logarithm zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L107).

Negating a real input leaves Lean’s real logarithm unchanged. This records the deliberate extension log x=log|x| away from zero, rather than a property of a complex logarithm. The identity also includes zero, since both sides then use log 0=0. It explains why later logarithm identities can permit negative nonzero factors. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L121).

The logarithm of a product is the sum of the logarithms whenever both real factors are nonzero. Negative factors are allowed because Lean applies the classical logarithm to absolute values, and absolute values multiply. The nonzero assumptions matter: multiplying zero by 2 gives logarithm zero, whereas log 0+log 2 is positive. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L133).

For nonzero real numerator and denominator, the logarithm of their quotient equals the numerator’s logarithm minus the denominator’s. Either sign is allowed through the absolute-value extension. Zero denominators are excluded despite Lean defining division by zero: for example, 2/0=0 has logarithm zero, whereas log 2−log 0 is positive. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L138).

The logarithm of a real reciprocal is the negative of the original logarithm. This holds for every real input, including negative values through the absolute-value extension. It even holds at zero: Lean defines 0⁻¹=0 and log 0=0, so both sides vanish. Thus this particular identity needs no nonzero hypothesis. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L143).

For any real x and natural number n, log(x^n)=n log x. Negative bases are permitted because logarithm discards their sign; zero bases also satisfy the identity under log 0=0. When n=0, the left side is log 1=0. The multiplier n is cast to the reals; the exponent here is natural, not arbitrary real. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L288).

The logarithm of a finite product equals the sum of the logarithms when every included real factor is nonzero. Negative factors are allowed by the absolute-value extension. The empty case is included: its product is 1 and its sum is zero. This is a finite identity, with no assertion about convergence of infinite products. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L408).

For a nonnegative real x, the logarithm of its nonnegative square root equals half of log x. Division by 2 is real division, not rounding. Zero is included because both logarithms are assigned zero there. Negative inputs are excluded: Lean’s square root becomes zero, while its logarithm extension can still have a nonzero value. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L303).

A real number at least 1 has nonnegative natural logarithm. The hypothesis automatically places the input in the positive domain, where logarithm increases from log 1=0. This is a sufficient condition, not a global classification of the extended function: Lean also assigns logarithm zero to zero, and negative inputs can have nonnegative logarithms. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L213).

A real number between zero and 1, inclusive, has nonpositive logarithm in Lean. For inputs strictly between those endpoints, this is the classical negative logarithm. At 1 the value is zero, and at zero it is also zero by the chosen extension. The inclusion of zero therefore does not assert a finite classical logarithm there. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L222).

A real input strictly greater than 1 has strictly positive natural logarithm. This is the usual comparison with log 1=0 on the positive axis. The strict inequality excludes the equality case at 1. It is not a necessary condition over all real inputs, because Lean’s absolute-value extension also gives positive logarithms to inputs below −1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L188).

For a real input strictly between zero and 1, the natural logarithm is strictly negative. Both endpoint exclusions are substantive in Lean: log 1=0 classically, while log 0=0 is its assigned extension. The statement concerns a positive input with a negative logarithm; its name does not mean that the input itself is negative. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L201).

The logarithm preserves a strict comparison x<y when x is positive; positivity of y then follows automatically. This is strict increase on the positive axis, not on all real numbers under Lean’s extension. Allowing x=0 would already fail: log 0=0 is larger, not smaller, than the negative logarithm of 1/2. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L155).

The logarithm preserves weak order between positive real numbers. Lean only asks explicitly that the smaller input be positive; the larger input’s positivity follows from their comparison. Equality is permitted. The hypothesis cannot simply be weakened to nonnegativity, since the assigned log 0=0 exceeds the logarithm of any positive number below 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L151).

For every real x, the logarithm of x/x is zero. When x is nonzero, the quotient is 1 and the result is the familiar log 1=0. At zero, Lean instead uses 0/0=0 and log 0=0. The unrestricted conclusion is therefore correct without asserting that x/x always equals 1. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L111).

The logarithm of any natural number, viewed as a real number, is nonnegative. Positive naturals are at least 1, so this follows from the usual positive-domain comparison. Natural zero is included separately using Lean’s assignment log 0=0. The cast is the exact inclusion of natural numbers into the reals, with no rounding operation. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/Log/Basic.lean#L225).

This is the ordinary real exponential e^x for every real x. Lean constructs the complex exponential from the convergent series ∑x^n/n!, then takes its real part at a real input; the imaginary part there is zero. The result is strictly positive, including for negative x, and no exceptional input or assigned default is needed. Compared with [Lebl Example 6.2.14](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_liminter.html#example_exponentialbypowerseries) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L81).

The real exponential takes the value 1 at zero. This is the standard normalization of e^x, also obtained from its defining power series: the constant term is 1 and all positive-degree terms vanish. There is no exceptional zero-input convention here; zero belongs to the classical domain just like every other real number. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L210).

The exponential turns the sum of any two real numbers into the product of their exponentials. Both inputs may be negative, zero, or positive; no sign or nonzero assumptions are needed. In particular, opposite inputs give reciprocal values because their sum is zero and exp 0=1. This is the ordinary real exponential addition law. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L212).

Negating a real exponent takes the reciprocal of its exponential. This holds for every real x because exp x is always positive and hence never zero. The inverse is ordinary real reciprocal, not a negative value or a logarithm. At x=0, both sides are 1, so no special division-by-zero branch is used. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L241).

The exponential of a difference equals the quotient of the two exponentials, for arbitrary real inputs. The denominator cannot vanish because every real exponential is positive. Thus the formula uses ordinary exact real division and needs no denominator hypothesis or rounding convention. Equal inputs give 1 on both sides, even when their common value is zero. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L244).

For a real x and a natural n, exp(n x) equals the ordinary nth power of exp x. The natural multiplier is first cast to the reals, so the multiplication is exact real arithmetic. Natural zero is included: exp 0=1 matches the zeroth power. Negative x is allowed, since the exponential remains positive. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L234).

For a finite set of indices, exponentiating the sum of real entries equals the product of their exponentials. The entries may have any signs, and no nonzero hypotheses are needed. The empty set gives exp 0=1, matching the empty product. The statement concerns finite sums and products, with no infinite-series convergence claim. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L227).

The exponential of every real number is strictly positive, including when the exponent is negative. It may become arbitrarily small as the exponent decreases, but its value is never zero at any finite real input. Lean’s real numbers here are exact mathematical reals, so numerical underflow is not part of this assertion. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L284).

A real exponential never vanishes, regardless of the sign of its exponent. This justifies cancelling it or using it as a denominator without a hypothesis on the input. The statement concerns finite real inputs; the fact that exp x tends to zero as x tends to negative infinity does not supply a real input where it vanishes. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L238).

The real exponential is strictly increasing on the whole real line: whenever x<y, exp x<exp y. There is no positivity restriction on either input, and negative exponents are included. Strict increase also guarantees that two different real inputs cannot have the same exponential value, without any interval restriction. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L300).

Equal real exponential values force equal real inputs. This follows from strict increase on the entire real line, so no sign restrictions or interval choices are required. The assertion is specifically about the real exponential; periodicity of the complex exponential does not contradict it, because the inputs here are real rather than arbitrary complex numbers. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L320).

Comparing two real exponentials with ≤ is equivalent to comparing their exponents with ≤. This gives both preservation and reflection of weak order for arbitrary real inputs, including negative values and equality. Consequently an exponential inequality can be cancelled in either direction without taking logarithms or supplying separate positivity assumptions on the inputs. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L317).

A strict inequality between two real exponentials holds exactly when the same strict inequality holds between their exponents. This applies on the whole real line, not just to positive inputs. Strictness matters: equal exponents produce equal outputs, so neither strict comparison holds. The equivalence reflects the exponential’s strict increase and injectivity. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L313).

A real exponential is at most 1 exactly when its exponent is nonpositive. Negative exponents give values below 1, while exponent zero gives 1. The comparison therefore includes its equality boundary deliberately. There is no hidden positivity assumption on the exponent; positivity is a property of the exponential’s output, not of its input. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L340).

The exponential of a real number is strictly below 1 exactly when that number is negative. Its value remains strictly positive, so the conclusion places it between zero and 1. Exponent zero is excluded because exp 0=1. This is a strict comparison on ordinary real numbers, with no zero or infinity endpoint assignment. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L337).

A real exponential is at least 1 exactly when its exponent is nonnegative. Zero is included and gives equality, while positive exponents give values strictly greater than 1. This is an equivalence, so an output bound also recovers the sign of the exponent; it is stronger than a one-way sufficient condition. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L344).

A real exponential exceeds 1 exactly when its exponent is positive. Thus strict positivity of the exponent is both sufficient and necessary for this particular output comparison. Zero gives equality instead, and negative exponents give values below 1. The theorem is about being above 1, not merely about the exponential being positive. Compared with [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L332).

For all real x, exp x≥1+x, with equality only at zero. This global bound follows from the mean value theorem: the derivative of exp x−x−1 is exp x−1, which has the sign of x. Negative inputs are included, even when the linear lower bound becomes nonpositive. Derived from [Lebl Theorem 4.2.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_mvt.html), [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html), and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L633).

For every nonzero real x, exp x>1+x. The hypothesis permits negative inputs; only zero is excluded. By the mean value theorem, exp x−x−1 has a strict minimum at zero because its derivative exp x−1 has the sign of x. At zero both sides instead equal 1. Derived from [Lebl Theorem 4.2.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_mvt.html), [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html), and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L624).

For every real x, exp(−x)≥1−x. Apply the tangent bound to −x: that bound follows from the mean value theorem since exp t−t−1 has derivative exp t−1, with the sign of t. Subtraction is real, so 1−x becomes negative for x>1; it is not truncated to zero. Derived from [Lebl Theorem 4.2.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_mvt.html), [Lebl §5.4](https://www.jirka.org/ra/html/sec_logandexp.html), and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Analysis/Complex/Exponential.lean#L641).
